prompt.context: Your client, Congo.com (named after one of Earth's rainforests), is one of the largest e-commerce retailers in the world. It specializes in a diverse logistics network, and its brand is built around consumer satisfaction. The company has grown dramatically over the last 5 years, but has started to notice recent profit margin dips. You have been hired to find the root causes that Congo must address to focus on profitability so they can continue to drive growth.
prompt.question: What are the root causes of Congo.com's declining profit margins, and what changes should Congo make to improve profitability? Quantify the impact of your recommended changes.

clarifying_info.q: What does Congo prioritize for customers?
clarifying_info.a: Congo gives its customers the best prices with the fastest delivery rates.

clarifying_info.q: Is this a global or domestic focus?
clarifying_info.a: Congo is a worldwide company, but wants to focus on US profitability to drive expansion into other countries.

clarifying_info.q: How many distribution facilities does Congo have in the US?
clarifying_info.a: There are eight main distribution facilities in the United States.

clarifying_info.q: How has Congo grown relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Company growth has outpaced all competitors in the retail industry.
Any positive change in profitability is the goal. It is up to you to quantify the impact of changes recommended.
Profit margin = net income / total revenue.

exhibits.title: Congo.com Income Statement (US Distribution Centers only, Unaudited, in millions)
exhibits.shows: A five-year income statement (2013–2017) for Congo.com's US distribution centers showing operating revenue (units shipped and average $/unit), total revenue, and operating expenses broken into Maintenance, SG&A, Transportation, Permitting, and Other, followed by NI Pre Tax, Taxes, and Net Income.

exhibits.title: Congo.com US Distribution Network – 2017
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing seven US distribution facilities (ABE8, AVP1, CLT2, CVG3, FTW1, MDW2, ONT8) on three metrics: Units per day, Operating Costs ($/day), and Transportation Costs ($/day). Each facility's square footage is also labeled.

exhibits.title: Trailer Utilization for >5 Year Old Facilities (with Project Proposal)
exhibits.shows: A combined bar-and-line chart showing Daily Trailers Shipped (bars, left axis) and Trailer Utilization % (line, right axis) from 2013 to 2017, alongside a table of facility ages and a project proposal box describing an automation upgrade option.

project_proposal.description: Automation upgrades would allow under-performing facilities to improve trailer utilization to Company standards. Current automation standards were implemented in all facilities built within the last 5 years.

framework: Revenue analysis: units shipped (growing ~30% YoY), average $/unit (fluctuating, largely market-driven), total revenue trajectory
Cost structure analysis: break down each cost line as % of revenue — identify which lines are growing disproportionately
Identify Transportation as the key driver: Transportation rose from 40% of revenue in 2013–2015 to 50% in 2016 and 60% in 2017
Facility-level deep dive: compare distribution centers on output, operating costs, and transportation costs to isolate underperformers
Root cause of transportation cost increase: lane costs, trailer utilization, and US DOT costs; focus on trailer utilization as the controllable lever
Quantify improvement opportunity from automation upgrade at eligible facilities
Recommendation: invest in automation at underperforming older facilities, project impact to net income, and consider further operational improvements

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell you about Congo's profitability trend and the primary driver of the margin decline?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute or recognize expense-as-%-of-revenue trends. Net income margin peaked at 5.6% in 2015–2016 and fell to 2.16% in 2017. Revenue grew 19% in 2017 but NI fell from $651M to $300M. Transportation is the culprit: it went from 40% of revenue (2013–2015) to 50% (2016) to 60% (2017). All other lines are flat or declining as a % of revenue. Avg $/unit changes are market-driven and largely outside Congo's control. Units shipped grow steadily at ~30% YoY.

math.setup: Compute key line items as % of total revenue for 2016 and 2017
math.answer: Transportation costs jumped from 50% to 60% of revenue in one year; this is the primary driver of margin compression.

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 2, which facility or facilities represent the biggest transportation cost opportunity, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that FTW1 ships the most units/day despite having only 500k sq ft (highest productivity at 4 units/sq ft). FTW1 and AVP1 both have Transportation Cost % of 80% vs 60% for all other five facilities. Strong candidates identify both FTW1 and AVP1. Bonus: AVP1 is easy to miss because it ships fewer units than other facilities. FTW1 is the highest-priority target due to volume; AVP1 is also eligible. MDW2 and ONT8 have 1M sq ft but are not outliers on transportation cost %.

questions.prompt: Exhibit 2 shows FTW1 has transportation costs of ~$1.6M/day and AVP1 has ~$1.2M/day. Facility transportation costs are composed of lane costs, trailer utilization, and US DOT costs. Congo has been expanding shipping destinations. Where should Congo focus?
questions.guidance: Lane costs and DOT costs naturally rise as Congo ships to more destinations — these are expected and semi-uncontrollable. Trailer utilization is the controllable lever. Candidate should push to investigate trailer utilization at FTW1 (and ideally AVP1). If candidate identifies trailer utilization as the key issue, give Exhibit 3.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 3 and the project proposal, calculate the annual transportation cost savings from implementing the automation upgrade. What is the impact on net income?
questions.guidance: Only facilities older than 5 years are eligible: AVP1 (7 years old) and FTW1 (8 years old). The upgrade cuts transportation costs by 25% at each eligible facility. Assume 350 operating days/year. Strong candidates identify both facilities; if only FTW1 is identified, calculate accordingly. Impact to NI pre-tax is additive to 2017 NI.

math.setup: Identify eligible facilities (>5 years old), apply 25% saving to their daily transportation costs, multiply by 350 operating days
math.answer: Both facilities: $245M/year in savings, boosting NI from $429M to ~$674M (~60% increase). Payback < 1 month on $20M investment.

questions.prompt: (Bonus/stretch) If trailer utilization is improved from 40% to 60% in 2017, what would the new number of daily trailers shipped be?
questions.guidance: Use the volume constant approach. At 40% utilization, 1400 trailers are shipped. The formula is: trailers = volume_constant * (1 + (1 - utilization)). Solve for volume constant, then apply 60% utilization.

math.setup: Trailer Utilization = % of truck trailer filled by actual SKU volume. (1 - Utilization) = unused space. Trailers shipped = volume_constant * (1 + (1 - utilization))
math.answer: 1,225 trailers per day (down from 1,407), reflecting higher efficiency per trailer.

recommendation: Congo should invest $20M in automation upgrades at AVP1 and FTW1 — the two facilities older than 5 years — to improve trailer utilization to Company standards
This will cut transportation costs by 25% at both sites, generating ~$245M in annual savings and increasing net income by ~60% (from $429M to ~$674M)
Implement productivity practices observed at high-efficiency facilities (e.g., FTW1's 4 units/sq ft output rate) across the broader network to improve throughput at under-utilized 1M sq ft sites
Further automation investments could reduce SG&A costs as facilities become more self-sufficient
risks: Implementation costs and potential disruption to current operations during the upgrade period
Dependency on US Department of Transportation regulations which are outside Congo's control
Higher automation may increase maintenance costs over time
Risk of cost overruns on the $10M/facility upgrade
next_steps: Engage logistics consultants to renegotiate trailer contracts and improve lane rate efficiency
Prepare distribution network infrastructure for higher trailer utilization and increased daily throughput
Evaluate remaining five facilities for future automation upgrades as they age beyond 5 years
Explore whether further automation can reduce SG&A costs across all facilities
